questions.stem: A patient, Rajesh with a history of wheezing, coughing and shortness of breath is being evaluated in the asthma clinic. Several drug treatments with different routes are under consideration. Which of the following statements about routes of administration is most correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Administration of a bronchodilator drug by inhaled aerosol is usually associated with more adverse effects than administration of this drug by mouth

options.label: B
options.text: Bioavailability of most drugs is greater with rectal administration than with sublingual administration

options.label: C
options.text: Administration of a drug by transdermal patch is often faster but is associated with more first pass metabolism than oral administration

options.label: D
options.text: The first pass effect is the result of elimination of a drug after administration and before it enters systemic circulation

questions.answerText: The first pass effect is the result of elimination of a drug after administration and before it enters systemic circulation
questions.solutionHtml:
patic portal circulation.

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. is incorrect because inhaled aerosol administration of bronchodilator drugs is associated with fewer adverse effects than oral administration, as it allows for targeted delivery of the drug to the site of action in the lungs, with minimal systemic absorption.

 

Option B. is incorrect because sublingual administration generally results in greater bioavailability than rectal administration, as the sublingual route allows for rapid absorption of the drug into the bloodstream through the rich network of blood vessels under the tongue, bypassing the first-pass metabolism in the liver.

 

Option C. is incorrect because transdermal administration of a drug is associated with slower onset of action than oral administration, as the drug must penetrate the skin barrier to enter systemic circulation.

 

Educational objective:

 

First pass effect refers to the metabolism of a drug within the liver that significantly reduces the bioavailability of the drug before it reaches systemic circulation, as opposed to comparing routes of administration and their impact on drug delivery and metabolism.

questions.stem: All the following factors tend to increase the volume of distribution of a drug EXCEPT:

options.label: B
options.text: Low ionization at physiological pH values

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) High plasma protein binding.

 

Option A:

 

  • When a drug binds extensively to plasma proteins, such as albumin, its ability to leave the bloodstream and distribute into other tissues is reduced. This leads to a lower Vd because a greater proportion of the drug remains confined to the plasma.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Low ionization at physiological pH values: Drugs that are less ionized at physiological pH can more readily cross cell membranes since non-ionized forms are generally more lipid-soluble. This allows the drug to distribute more widely into various tissues, including those beyond the vascular compartment, thus increasing the Vd.

 

Option C. High lipid solubility: Lipid-soluble drugs can cross cell membranes more easily and can accumulate in fatty tissues. This property can lead to a larger Vd because the drug can be distributed more extensively into body tissues, particularly fat stores.

 

Option D. High tissue binding: When a drug has a high affinity for tissue binding sites, it will be sequestered in these peripheral compartments rather than remaining in the bloodstream. This sequestration in tissues increases the Vd as the drug is stored outside of the vascular system.

 

Educational Objective:

 

While high lipid solubility, low ionization, and high tissue binding increase a drug's volume of distribution, high plasma protein binding generally decreases it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of the clinical importance of enzyme induction?

options.label: A
options.text: Phenobarbitone is used in the treatment of neonatal jaundice

options.label: B
options.text: Phenytoin is contraindicated in acute intermittent porphyria

options.label: C
options.text: Tolerance occurs to anticonvulsant action of carbamazepine in few doses

options.label: D
options.text: Omeprazole increases metabolism and thus inhibits the action of clopidogrel

questions.answerText: Omeprazole increases metabolism and thus inhibits the action of clopidogrel
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Omeprazole increases the metabolism and thus inhibits the action of clopidogrel.

 

Option D:

 

Omeprazole inhibits the activity of CYP2C19, which is responsible for the conversion of clopidogrel to its active form. This can lead to decreased efficacy of clopidogrel and potentially increase the risk of cardiovascular events. This is an example of the clinical importance of enzyme inhibition. The other options are all examples of the clinical importance of enzyme induction.

 

Other Options

 

Option A. Phenobarbitone is used in the treatment of neonatal jaundice: Correct .  Phenobarbitone induces certain liver enzymes, increasing the metabolism of bilirubin, which can help in the treatment of neonatal jaundice by facilitating the elimination of bilirubin from the body.

 

Option B. Phenytoin is contraindicated in acute intermittent porphyria: Correct. Phenytoin induces hepatic enzymes, and this induction can exacerbate acute intermittent porphyria, a condition where porphyrin metabolism is disturbed.

 

Option C. Tolerance occurs to anticonvulsant action of carbamazepine in few doses: Correct, to an extent. Carbamazepine is known to induce its own metabolism over time, which can lead to tolerance as the body becomes more efficient at breaking down the drug, necessitating dose adjustments.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

The concept of enzyme induction is clinically important, as it can inform treatment decisions, such as using phenobarbitone for neonatal jaundice due to its inducing effects, avoiding phenytoin in porphyria, and being aware of potential tolerance to drugs like carbamazepine. Conversely, enzyme inhibition, such as the interaction between omeprazole and clopidogrel, can significantly impact drug efficacy.

questions.stem: The extent to which ionization of a drug takes place is dependent upon pKa of the drug and the pH of the solution in which the drug is dissolved. Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.label: A
options.text: pKa of a drug is the pH at which the drug is 50% ionized

options.label: B
options.text: Small changes of pH near the pKa of a weak acidic drug will not affect its degree of ionization

options.label: C
options.text: Knowledge of pKa of a drug is useful in predicting its behavior in various body fluids

options.label: D
options.text: Phenobarbitone with a pKa of 7.2 is largely unionized at acid pH and will be about 40% non-ionized in plasma

questions.answerText: Small changes of pH near the pKa of a weak acidic drug will not affect its degree of ionization
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Small changes of pH near the pKa of a weak acidic drug will not affect its degree of ionization

 

Small changes in pH near the pKa value of a drug can significantly affect its ionization, especially for weak acids and bases. Because the relationship between pH and ionization is logarithmic, even small changes in pH can lead to significant shifts in the ratio of ionized to unionized drug. For example, if the pH is decreased from 7.4 to 7.2, the degree of ionization of a weak acidic drug with a pKa of 7.4 will increase from 50% to 75%.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. pKa of a drug is the pH at which the drug is 50% ionized: Correct. pKa is indeed the pH at which a drug exists as 50% ionized and 50% unionized. This is an important property because it determines the drug's ionization at different pH levels, which affects its absorption, distribution, and elimination.

 

Option C. Knowledge of pKa of a drug is useful in predicting its behavior in various body fluids: Correct. Understanding the pKa of a drug allows for predictions about where the drug will be absorbed (stomach vs. intestine), how it will distribute in the body, and how it might be reabsorbed in the renal tubules or secreted into the stomach.

 

Option D. Phenobarbitone with a pKa of 7.2 is largely unionized at acid pH and will be about 40% non-ionized in plasma: Phenobarbitone is a barbiturate (acidic drug) and has a pKa of 7.2, which is higher than the pH of plasma (7.4). Therefore, it will be unionized a little less than 50 percent in plasma (drug is acidic and medium is basic as compared to pKa) and is about 40% non-ionized. On the other hand, in acidic medium more will be non-ionized as the medium is also acidic and drug is also acidic.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • The ionization of a drug in the body is critical to its pharmacokinetics and can be predicted by knowing the pKa of the drug and the pH of the environment; however, small changes in pH near the pKa can significantly affect the drug's ionization state.

questions.stem: A 70 Kg person was started on a drug with Vd =10 L and exhibits first-order elimination kinetics. The rate of drug clearance is calculated to be 6.93 L/hr. It is determined that repeating the second dose when 75% of the drug is eliminated will minimize toxicity while maintaining trough levels above the minimum inhibitory concentration. Based on these research findings, which of the following is the most appropriate dosing interval for this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
pan style="font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif">Ans. B) 2 hours

 

Explanation:

 

To determine the dosing interval for this drug, we need to first calculate the half-life (t1/2) of the drug. We can use the formula:

t1/2 = 0.693 x Vd / clearance

 

where Vd is the volume of distribution and clearance is the rate of drug clearance.

Substituting the given values, we get:

t1/2 = 0.693 x 10 / 6.93 t1/2 = 1 hour

 

The time to eliminate 75% of the drug would be 2 half-lives (in 1 half-life 50 percent is eliminated and in 2 half-lives 75 percent will be eliminated) . Therefore, the time to eliminate 75% of the drug would be:

t = 2 x t1/2 = 2 x 1 = 2 hours

 

So, the appropriate dosing interval would be around 2 hours to ensure that 75% of the previous dose is eliminated before the next dose is given.

 

Educational Objective:

 

For a drug with first-order elimination kinetics, a dosing interval should be set based on its half-life to minimize toxicity and maintain effective drug concentrations.



ore, the time to eliminate 75% of the drug would be:

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs should be given in sustained release oral dosage form?

options.label: A
options.text: An anti-arrhythmic drug with a plasma half-life of 10 seconds used for acute treatment of PSVT.

options.label: B
options.text: An anti-inflammatory drug with a plasma half-life of 24 hr

options.label: C
options.text: A hypnotic drug with a plasma half-life of 2 hours

options.label: D
options.text: An antihypertensive with a plasma half-life of 3 hours

questions.answerText: An antihypertensive with a plasma half-life of 3 hours
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) An antihypertensive with a plasma half-life of 3 hours

 

Sustained release (SR) oral dosage forms are designed to release the drug over an extended period to maintain therapeutic drug concentrations in the blood for a longer duration. Therefore, the ideal candidates for making a sustained release formulation are:

 

  • Drugs with a short plasma half-life
  • The drug used for a condition where prolonged therapy is required.

 

An antihypertensive with a plasma half-life of 3 hours is suitable for a sustained release oral dosage form because this drug requires lifelong therapy and by making SR formulation, we can give the drug less frequently.

 

Other Options 

 

Option A: An anti-arrhythmic drug with a plasma half-life of 10 seconds used for acute treatment of PSVT would not be suitable for a sustained release oral dosage form since it needs to act quickly in an acute situation.

 

Option B: An anti-inflammatory drug with a plasma half-life of 24 hours will not require a SR formulation because the drug already has a long half-life.

 

Option C: A hypnotic drug with a plasma half-life of 2 hours would not be suitable for a sustained release oral dosage form since hypnotics are required to work for 5-6 hours only and an SR form may result in prolonged sleep.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Sustained release oral dosage forms are most appropriate for drugs that have a short plasma half-life and are used for chronic conditions, such as an antihypertensive with a 3-hour half-life, to maintain consistent therapeutic levels and improve patient compliance with less frequent dosing.

questions.stem: A new drug Z is being tested in animals for Anti-diabetic activity. When drug Z was given in a dose of 10 mg, 50 mice got the expected effect among the 100 who received the drug. However, at 100 mg dose, half of the animals died. Which of the following statements about drug Z is INCORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: The final dose of drug Z in humans should be between 10 mg and 100 mg

options.label: B
options.text: ED50 of drug Z is 10 mg

options.label: C
options.text: LD50 of drug Z is 100 mg

options.label: D
options.text: Therapeutic index of drug Z is around 10

questions.answerText: The final dose of drug Z in humans should be between 10 mg and 100 mg
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) The final dose of drug Z in humans should be between 10 mg and 100 mg.

 

Option A:

 

The final dose of drug Z in humans cannot be determined solely based on the animal data provided. Animal studies are only the first step in the drug development process, and further studies are needed to determine the appropriate human dose. Other factors, such as pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety profile in humans, also need to be taken into consideration.



Other Options:

Option B: ED50 is the dose at which 50% of the animals exhibit the desired effect. In this case, the ED50 of drug Z is 10 mg, which means that 50% of the mice experienced the expected effect at a dose of 10 mg.

 

Option C: LD50 is the dose at which 50% of the animals die. In this case, the LD50 of drug Z 100 mg, as half of the animals died at this dose.

 

Option D: Therapeutic index (TI) is the ratio of the LD50 to the ED50. It is a measure of the safety of the drug, with a higher TI indicating a safer drug. The TI of drug Z can be calculated as:

 

TI = LD50/ED50

TI = 100/10 = 10

Therefore, the therapeutic index of drug Z is around 10, which indicates that it is relatively safe.

 

 

Educational Objective:

 

The therapeutic index (TI) of drug Z is 10, determined by the ratio of the LD50 (dose lethal to 50% of subjects) to the ED50 (dose effective in 50% of subjects), but the appropriate dose for humans cannot be extrapolated directly from animal data without further clinical investigation.



ore, the therapeutic index of drug Z is around 10, which indicates that it is relatively safe.

questions.stem: Experiments show that 50% of an oral 100-mg dose of Drug A is absorbed in a 60-kg test subject. However, the fractional bioavailability was only 0.2. Assuming a liver blood flow of 1500 mL/min, which of the following is the hepatic clearance of Drug A in this situation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Explanation:

 

Let us do the calculations based on the given Information:

 

This question can be solved by two methods.

 

Method 1- by using the formula

 

Dose = 100 mg
 

Fraction absorbed (F_abs) = 0.5
 

Fractional bioavailability (F) = 0.2
 

Liver blood flow (Q) = 1500 mL/min
 

Systemic bioavailability(F)=Fractional absorption*(1–Extraction ratio)

 

0.2=0.5×(1−ER)

 

0.4=1-ER

 

ER=0.6

 

Now, hepatic clearance is calculated as:

 

clearance=ER*Hepatic blood flow

 

=0.6*1500ml/min

 

=900ml/min

 

Method 2- by using the conceptual knowledge.

 

  1. Absorption and Bioavailability:
    • 50% of the 100 mg dose of Drug A is absorbed, so 50 mg reaches the liver.
    • The fractional bioavailability (F) is 0.2, meaning 20% of the absorbed drug reaches the systemic circulation, or 20 mg.
  2. Amount Extracted by the Liver:
    • 50 mg of the absorbed drug reaches the liver, and 20 mg exits into the systemic circulation.
    • Therefore, the amount extracted by the liver is: 50 mg − 20  mg = 30 mg
  3. Hepatic Extraction Ratio (ER):
    • The hepatic extraction ratio is the fraction of the drug extracted by the liver:
    • ER = Amount extracted by the liver/Amount reaching the liver = 30 mg / 50 mg = 0.6
  4. Hepatic Clearance (Clₕ):
    • Hepatic clearance is given by the formula:
    • CL = Liver Blood Flow (Q) × Extraction Ratio 
    • Given that the liver blood flow (Q) is 1500 mL/min (or 1.5 L/min) and the extraction ratio (ER) is 0.6:
    • CL = 1500 mL/min × 0.6 = 900 mL/min

 

Educational Objective:

 

To calculate the hepatic clearance of a drug, apply the formula hepatic clearance = hepatic extraction ratio × hepatic blood flow, using the fraction of the drug dose absorbed and the fractional bioavailability to determine the extraction ratio.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following figures correctly represent the relationship between clearance and plasma concentration for a drug following first order kinetics?
questions.solutionHtml:

  • Figure a represents a scenario where clearance is independent of plasma concentration. This is consistent with first-order kinetics, where a constant fraction of the drug is eliminated per unit time.
  • Figure b suggests that clearance increases linearly with increasing plasma concentration, which would imply dose-dependent kinetics, not first-order kinetics.
  • Figure c and d both show clearance changing with plasma concentration, which suggests non-linear kinetics.

Educational Objective:

 

In first-order kinetics, the clearance of a drug remains constant regardless of plasma concentration, which is depicted as a horizontal line parallel to the plasma concentration axis in a graph of clearance versus plasma concentration.

questions.stem: Phenytoin is a drug that follows zero order kinetics at high doses and first order kinetics at low doses. Suppose 400 mg phenytoin is present in the body and its rate of elimination at this dose is 200 mg/hr., how much will remain in plasma after 2 hours?

options.label: D
options.text: Cannot be predicted from this information

questions.answerText: Cannot be predicted from this information
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Cannot be predicted from this information.

 

  • In zero order kinetics, the rate of elimination is constant. However, it is dependent (directly proportional) on plasma concentration in first order kinetics.
  • At high dose, phenytoin follows zero order kinetics but at low dose it follows first- order kinetics.
  • As the question does not mention that at what plasma concentration, the kinetic will change from zero order to first order, we cannot predict how much will remain in plasma.

 

Educational Objective:

 

For drugs like phenytoin, which exhibit zero-order kinetics at higher doses and first-order kinetics at lower doses, the specific plasma concentration at which this shift occurs must be known to accurately predict plasma levels after a given period.

Aspirin (t½ = 15 minutes):
Aspirin has a very short half-life, meaning it rapidly reaches steady-state levels with regular dosing. A loading dose is typically unnecessary because the drug accumulates quickly.

Acetaminophen (t½ = 2 hours):

questions.stem: Constant intravenous infusion (at a rate of 200 mg/hour) of a drug with half-life of 1 hour is started and plasma concentration is measured at different intervals. If steady state plasma concentration is 400 µg/dl, what was the likely plasma concentration at 2 hours’ time after starting the infusion?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) 300 µg/dl

 

1. By using the formula

 

In a constant rate infusion, the time to reach steady-state is mainly dependent on the half-life of the drug. After about 4-5 half-lives, the drug reaches approximately 93-97% of the steady-state. However, the plasma concentration at different time intervals can be calculated by:

 

Ct = Css (1 − e^−kt)

Where:
Ct is the plasma concentration at time t,
Css is the steady-state concentration,
k is the elimination rate constant, and
t is the time.

The relationship between the elimination rate constant (k) and the half-life (t½) is given by:

k = 0.693/ t½

Given t½ = 1 hour, k = 0.693.

At t = 2 hours:

C2 = 400 (1 − e^ −0.693×2)

Calculating:

C2 = 400 (1 − ^e − 1.386)

Using the value of e^-1.386 ≈ 0.25:

C2 = 400 (1 − 0.25)

C2 = 400 × 0.75

C2 = 300

Therefore, the plasma concentration at 2 hours after starting the infusion would be 300 μg/dl.

 

2. Logical method

 

  • The rate of increase of plasma concentration (when the drug is given by constant iv infusion) follows the same pattern when there is fall in plasma concentration (when the drug is stopped after achieving a particular concentration.
  • In 2 half-lives, the concentration of drug achieved should be 75 percent (50+25) of the steady state.
  • Thus, Concentration at 2 hours will be 400 X 75/100 = 300 mcg/dl.

 

Educational Objective:

 

During constant intravenous infusion, plasma concentration of a drug with a half-life of 1 hour at 2 hours is likely to be 75% of the steady-state concentration due to exponential accumulation.



ore, the plasma concentration at 2 hours after starting the infusion would be 300 μg/dl.

questions.stem: Time for peak plasma concentration (Tmax) indicates?
questions.solutionHtml:
ong>Tmax is an indicator of how quickly a drug reaches its peak concentration in the plasma after administration. A shorter Tmax suggests faster absorption into the systemic circulation.

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. The rate of elimination:  Incorrect. The rate of elimination is more closely related to the drug's half-life (t1/2), which is the time required for the plasma concentration of the drug to reduce to half its initial value. Tmax does not provide direct information about the rate at which the drug is eliminated from the body.

 

Option C. The duration of effect: Incorrect. The duration of effect of a drug is influenced by its half-life and the duration of interaction with its target receptors, not just the time to reach peak concentration. Tmax alone does not provide complete information about how long a drug's effects will last.

 

Option D. The extent of absorption: Incorrect. The extent of absorption is more accurately indicated by the area under the curve (AUC) or the total plasma concentration of the drug over time. Tmax tells us when the peak concentration occurs but does not indicate the total amount of drug absorbed.

 

Educational objective:

 

Tmax is a pharmacokinetic parameter that indicates the time at which a drug reaches its maximum concentration in plasma, reflecting the rate of absorption from the site of administration into the systemic circulation.



lecting the rate of absorption from the site of administration into the systemic circulation.

questions.stem: All of the following statements regarding steady state plasma concentration of a drug are true EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: At steady state, rate of administration of drug is equal to its rate of elimination

options.label: B
options.text: Steady state plasma concentration achieved depends upon half-life

options.label: C
options.text: Drugs with longer half-life can be given as loading dose to achieve steady state more quickly

options.label: D
options.text: Average steady state plasma concentration achieved is same irrespective of once daily or twice daily administration if total daily dose is same

questions.answerText: Steady state plasma concentration achieved depends upon half-life
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Steady state plasma concentration achieved depends upon half-life.

 

Option A. is true because at steady state, the rate of administration of a drug is equal to its rate of elimination.

 

Option B. is false because the steady-state plasma concentration achieved for a drug depends on dosing rate. Half life determines when that steady state concentration will reach.

 

Option C. is true because loading doses can be used to achieve steady state more quickly for drugs with longer half-lives.

 

Option D. The statement that the average steady state plasma concentration achieved is the same irrespective of once daily or twice daily administration if the total daily dose is the same is true. Steady state concentration achieved depends upon dosing rate. It means in total daily dose (dose per unit time) is same whether we give it once a day or twice a day, the steady state concentration acheived will be same.

questions.stem: A drug x is secreted through renal tubules, tubular secretion of this drug can be confirmed if renal clearance of drug x is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. More than the GFR

 

  • Renal clearance refers to the volume of blood plasma that is cleared of a particular substance by the kidneys per unit time. In the case of a drug that is secreted through the renal tubules, its renal clearance will be greater than the glomerular filtration rate (GFR).
  • The GFR represents the rate at which blood is filtered through the glomeruli of the kidneys. If a drug is only filtered by the glomeruli and not secreted by the renal tubules, its renal clearance would be equal to the GFR. However, if a drug is actively secreted by the renal tubules, its renal clearance will be greater than the GFR because the drug is being actively transported into the tubules in addition to being filtered by the glomeruli.
  • Therefore, if the renal clearance of drug X is greater than the GFR, it is a strong indication that the drug is being actively secreted by the renal tubules.


ers to the volume of blood plasma that is cleared of a particular substance by the kidneys per unit time. In the case of a drug that is secreted through the renal tubules, its renal clearance will be greater than the glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

questions.stem: A new drug is found to be highly lipid soluble. It is metabolized at a slower rate of 10% per hour. On intravenous injection it produces general anaesthesia that lasts only for 15 min. This short duration of anaesthesia is due to?

options.label: A
options.text: Metabolism of the drug in liver

options.label: B
options.text: High plasma protein binding of the drug

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Redistribution

 

  • The short duration of anesthesia produced by the highly lipid soluble drug on intravenous injection is due to redistribution.
  • Redistribution refers to the process by which a drug moves from one site of the body to another. In the case of general anesthesia, after the drug is administered, it rapidly distributes to the brain, where it produces its effects. However, due to its high lipid solubility, the drug also quickly moves out of the brain and into other body tissues, such as adipose tissue, where it becomes sequestered and inactive. This results in a rapid decline in the drug concentration in the brain, leading to the termination of anesthesia.
  • Metabolism of the drug in the liver, high plasma protein binding of the drug, and excretion of the drug by the kidney can all affect the duration of action of a drug, but they are not the primary reasons for the short duration of anesthesia in this case.


ers to the process by which a drug moves from one site of the body to another. In the case of general anesthesia, after the drug is administered, it rapidly distributes to the brain, where it produces its effects. However, due to its high lipid solubility, the drug also quickly moves out of the brain and into other body tissues, such as adipose tissue, where it becomes sequestered and inactive. This results in a rapid decline in the drug concentration in the brain, leading to the termination of anesthesia.

questions.stem: Oral loading dose of a drug depends on the following factors except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Clearance of the drug

 

  • The oral loading dose of a drug depends on the drug concentration to be achieved, the volume of distribution, and the bioavailability of the drug.
  • Loading dose = Vd X Target PC/F
  • Clearance of the drug is not directly related to the loading dose. Clearance is the rate at which the drug is eliminated from the body, and it is a factor that determines the maintenance dose of the drug.

questions.stem: A three-year-old child is brought to the emergency department having just ingested a large overdose of an antihistaminic drug. This drug is a weak base capable of entering most tissues including the brain. On physical examination the heart rate is 100/minute, blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg and the respiratory rate is 20/ minute. In this case of poisoning?

options.label: A
options.text: Urinary excretion would be accelerated by administration of NaHCO3, an alkalinizing agent

options.label: B
options.text: Urinary excretion would be accelerated by administration of NH4Cl, an acidifying agent

options.label: C
options.text: More of the drug would be ionized at blood pH than at stomach pH

options.label: D
options.text: Absorption of the drug would be faster from the stomach than from the small intestine.

questions.answerText: Urinary excretion would be accelerated by administration of NH4Cl, an acidifying agent
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B.  Urinary excretion would be accelerated by administration of NH4Cl, an acidifying agent.

 

  • In cases of drug overdose, enhancing drug elimination is an important aspect of management. For weakly basic drugs like antihistamines, urinary excretion is the primary route of elimination.
  • The pH gradient between the urine (acidic) and blood (basic) favors ion trapping of weak bases in the urine. This means that if the urine is made more acidic, more of the drug will be ionized and trapped in the urine, leading to faster elimination.
  • Administering an acidifying agent like NH4Cl can help in acidifying the urine and accelerating urinary excretion of the drug. On the other hand, administering an alkalinizing agent like NaHCO3 would have the opposite effect and slow down drug elimination.
  • Option (a) is incorrect because administering NaHCO3 would actually slow down drug elimination.
  • Option (c) is incorrect because weak bases are more non-ionized at basic pH (as in the blood) than at acidic pH (as in the stomach).
  • Option (d) is also incorrect because absorption of weak bases is actually faster from the small intestine than from the stomach due to the higher pH and larger surface area for absorption in the small intestine.

questions.stem: About first order kinetics true statement is?

options.label: B
options.text: Fixed amount of the drug is eliminated per unit time

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Clearance remains constant

 

 

  • Rate of elimination is constant in zero order kinetics. In first order kinetics, the rate of drug elimination is proportional to the drug concentration.
  • Option A. Clearance remains constant in first order kinetics is correct statement.
  • Option B. Fixed amount of the drug is eliminated per unit time in zero order kinetics whereas in first order kinetics constant fraction of a drug is eliminated per unit time.
  • Option C. Half-life increases with dose is also incorrect because in first order kinetics, the half-life of a drug is constant.

questions.stem: Drug X is normally administered to patients at a rate of 50 mg/hour. Elimination of the drug X from body takes place as: - Hepatic Metabolism 10% - Biliary Secretion 10% - Renal Excretion 80% This drug has to be administered to a 65 years old patient Uttam Singh, with a GFR of 60 ml/min. (assuming normal GFR is 120 ml/min). Liver and biliary functions are normal in this patient. What should be the dose rate of drug X in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. 30 mg/hour

 

  • In this patient, the renal function is 50 percent (GFR is 60 ml/min as compared to normal GFR of 120 ml/min. So, renal clearance of the drug will be half of normal. Hepatic and biliary clearance have not changed.
  • This means the dose rate of the drug should be 60 percent of normal dose rate (10% for hepatic + 10% for biliary + ½ of 80% for renal).
  • Normal dose rate of drug X is 50 mg/hour
  • So in this patient, the dose rate of drug X should be 50 x 0.6 = 30 mg/hour
